info.title: Flashduty Open API
info.description: Public HTTP API for the Flashduty incident management platform — incidents, notification templates, channels, schedules, monitors, RUM, and platform administration. Every operation is authenticated with an `app_key` query parameter issued from the Flashduty console under Account → APP Keys. Responses follow a uniform envelope: `{ request_id, data }` on success, `{ request_id, error }` on failure.

post.description: Run a synchronous ad-hoc query against a configured data source and return a stable `query_result.v1` result whose natural shape is frames, records, or samples. This public API requires monit-edge v0.65.0 or later.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **100 requests/minute**; **5 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | Any valid `app_key` (read-only; not gated by a specific permission class) |
| Edge requirement | Supported deployments require **monit-edge v0.65.0 or later** |

## Usage

- Treat **monit-edge v0.65.0** as the minimum supported Edge version for this public API. WebAPI retains migration adapters for older Edge versions: query.v2 results may still preserve frames, records, or samples, while legacy rows can expose only the information they retained. These adapters do not change the support floor; older protocols lack query.v3 cancellation and error-lifecycle semantics, and data already lost by legacy rows cannot be recovered.
- The public response format is always `query_result.v1` and is independent of the internal Edge query protocol. Dispatch on `result.kind` (`frames`, `records`, or `samples`); do not infer the result shape from `ds_type` or the Edge version.
- A `frames` result may contain multiple table or time-series frames. Field values are columnar and all fields in one frame have the same length.
- A `records` result may contain nested JSON and null records. Integer literals outside JavaScript's safe integer range are returned as decimal strings.
- A `samples` result contains label sets and instant values. A value may be a number or one of the strings `NaN`, `+Inf`, and `-Inf`.
- The final success response is limited to 8 MiB and query results are limited to 1,000 rows. Narrow the time range, reduce fields, or aggregate at the source when a request exceeds a limit.
- Query failures use non-2xx HTTP status codes and the standard error envelope. Do not transparently fall back to the deprecated `/monit/query/rows` endpoint.
- Query execution may take up to 35 seconds across WebAPI forwarding and Edge execution. Configure client timeouts to at least 40 seconds and propagate cancellation when the caller abandons a query.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **2,000 requests/minute**; **32 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Datasources Read** (`monit`) |

Use datasource IDs from `/monit/datasource/list`. Disabled datasources return `datasource_disabled`; `alerting_enabled=false` does not block tools. Errors use non-2xx HTTP status and `error.code`, `error.message`, `error.reason`. `tool_not_supported` indicates the selected executor does not provide this tool; it is not a vendor permission error. Never retry through another Edge or the legacy diagnose endpoint automatically.

## Usage

- Two tool families share this entry: diagnostic tools defined by the executing Edge (e.g. `mysql.overview`, `prometheus.metric_trends`) and query tools named `<type>.query`. The tool prefix must match the datasource type.
- Query tools require the Edge cluster to support Explore queries (protocol milestone v0.68.0); diagnostic tools require the v0.71.0 base invoke protocol. Unsupported clusters fail with `edge_upgrade_required`, `mixed_edge_versions`, or `edge_version_unknown`; never fall back to `/monit/query/data` or another endpoint automatically.
- For query tools, `params` follows the per-datasource schema named in the `tool` field description. `expr` and `execution` are always required. `limit`/`direction` only bound raw-log retrieval, never SQL rows or scanned data. Unknown extension fields are tolerated but never executed or forwarded.
- Query `data` is the complete Explore result: `format` is `explore_result.v1` and `result.kind` is `samples`, `frames`, or `logs`; log results keep `applied_limit` and `has_more`. Query results never synthesize `summary` or `truncated`.
- Request body limit 128 KiB; complete success response limit 10 MiB for both families; diagnostic tool timeout at most 25 seconds.

| Rate limits | **100 requests/minute**; **16 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Datasources Read** (`monit`) |

- Use this endpoint when you need the data source's native result shape; `/monit/query/data` returns the stable `query_result.v1` contract instead. Dispatch on `data.result.kind` (`frames`, `samples`, or `logs`) here.
- `execution.kind` decides which companion fields are accepted: `instant` needs only `to_ms`, `range` requires `from_ms`, `to_ms`, and `max_data_points`, and `window` takes `from_ms` and `to_ms`. `step_seconds` is not accepted; the step is derived from `max_data_points` and `min_step_seconds`.
- `args` carries macro substitutions such as Grafana-style variables; every value is a string.
- A `logs` result is capped at 1,000 entries and reports `applied_limit` plus `has_more`. Time-series and sample results are capped at 1,000 items each and the whole success response at 8 MiB.
- Query execution may take up to 35 seconds across WebAPI forwarding and Edge execution. Configure client timeouts to at least 40 seconds.

## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |

| Permissions | Any valid `app_key` (read-only; not gated by a specific permission class) |
| Edge requirement | Supported deployments require **monit-edge v0.35.0 or later** |

## Usage

- Pass the target data source in the `X-DSID` header. It must be a Prometheus-compatible data source owned by the authenticated account; use `/monit/datasource/list` to obtain its ID.
- The 200 body is the data source's native Prometheus HTTP API payload, **not** the standard `{ request_id, data }` envelope. Failures raised before the data source is reached are returned as `text/plain` with the matching 4xx or 5xx status.
- When `X-DSID` is omitted, the request falls back to the platform's own Prometheus proxy. Send the header to query a specific data source.

cron_pattern.description: Schedule expression: a 6-field cron (with seconds) or an `@every 30s` interval. Must not start with `CRON_TZ=` or `TZ=`; set the timezone in the `timezone` field instead.

timezone.description: Timezone the rule runs in; it decides how the cron schedule and enabled time windows are interpreted. Only IANA names are accepted (e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC`, `Europe/London`); abbreviations or offsets like `Local`, `UTC+8`, `CST` are rejected. Empty falls back to `Asia/Shanghai`.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds the evaluation query window is shifted back, compensating for data ingestion latency.

enabled_times.description: Time windows during which the rule is in effect. When omitted or empty, the rule is active 00:00–23:59 every day.

annotations.description: Extra annotation key-value pairs delivered with alert events; keys must not start with `$` (reserved for query fields).

description_type.description: Format of the description content. Empty or omitted defaults to `text`. `text` = plain text; `markdown` = Markdown, rendered as such in alert details.

channel_ids.description: Collaboration space IDs alerts are sent to. May be empty; alerts then route through the global integration.

repeat_interval.description: Notification repeat interval in seconds. Values below 1 fall back to the default 3600.

repeat_total.description: Maximum number of repeat notifications. Values below 1 fall back to the default 3.

investigation_targets.description: Drill-down entries linked from the alert event detail page; at most 20 items, duplicates rejected. On update the field is presence-based: omit it to keep the current value, pass `[]` to clear.

creator_id.description: Creator member ID, filled by the server from the current user; any client-supplied value is ignored.

creator_name.description: Creator name, filled by the server; any client-supplied value is ignored.

updater_id.description: ID of the member who last updated the rule, filled by the server; any client-supplied value is ignored.

updater_name.description: Name of the member who last updated the rule, filled by the server; any client-supplied value is ignored.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp in seconds, generated by the server; any client-supplied value is ignored.

updated_at.description: Last update time as a Unix timestamp in seconds, generated by the server; any client-supplied value is ignored.

queries.description: Query list with at least one entry; each needs a unique `name` (`R` and `__all__` are reserved) and a non-empty, non-duplicated `expr`.

name.description: Query identifier (e.g. `A`), must match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; `R` and `__all__` are reserved and cannot be used.

expr.description: Query expression.

label_fields.description: Result fields used as alert event labels; rows with the same label set form one alert. Must not overlap `value_fields`; applies to tabular results (SQL/ES-like datasources).

value_fields.description: Numeric result fields evaluated by threshold expressions (referenced as `$A.<field>`); required for threshold checks when the datasource is not `prometheus`/`loki`/`victorialogs`. Field names must not contain `.`.

args.description: Datasource-specific query parameters; keys follow the `<datasource>.<param>` convention (e.g. `es.type`, `tencent_cls.limit`). Most datasources need none.

relate_queries.description: Optional auxiliary queries whose results attach to alert events as context. Each entry needs a unique `name` (not colliding with any query name) and a non-empty `expr`.

name.description: Auxiliary query identifier.

expr.description: Query expression.

args.description: Datasource-specific parameters for the auxiliary query; same convention as `queries[].args`.

check_anydata.description: Any-data check configuration: fires when a query returns any data row. See `AlertRuleAnyDataV2`.

enabled.description: Whether the threshold check is enabled.

alerting_check_times.description: Fire after the alert condition is met this many times; when enabled, minimum 1 and maximum 10000. Combined with `alerting_window_size` it means at least N hits within the last M evaluations.

alerting_window_size.description: Optional sliding window size M: fire only when the condition is met at least `alerting_check_times` times within the last M evaluations. Omit for consecutive mode (N consecutive hits). Must satisfy `alerting_check_times` <= M <= 10000.

recovery_check_times.description: Recover after the recovery condition is met this many times; minimum 1 when enabled.

critical.description: Critical threshold expression referencing query results as `$<query>` or `$<query>.<value_field>`, e.g. `$A > 90`; when enabled at least one of the three severities must be set.

warning.description: Warning threshold expression; same syntax as `critical`.

info.description: Info threshold expression; same syntax as `critical`.

recovery_mode.description: How recovery is decided (lifecycle v2); required when enabled. `condition_clear` = recover once the alert expression no longer holds; `recovery` is not allowed. `expression_match` = recover when the `recovery.expr` threshold expression holds. `recovery_query_match` = recover when the `recovery.expr` query expression evaluates true. `manual` = never recover automatically; alerts need manual handling, no recovery event is pushed, and `recovery` is not allowed.

recovery.description: Recovery evaluation config. Required (with non-empty `recovery.expr`) only when `recovery_mode` is `expression_match` or `recovery_query_match`; must be omitted for the other modes.

AlertRuleAnyDataV2.description: Any-data check configuration (lifecycle v2). Fires when a query returns any data row.

enabled.description: Whether the any-data check is enabled: any returned data row triggers an alert.

alerting_check_times.description: Fire after the alert condition is met this many times; when enabled, minimum 1 and maximum 10000. Combined with `alerting_window_size` it means at least N hits within the last M evaluations.

alerting_window_size.description: Optional sliding window size M: fire only when the condition is met at least `alerting_check_times` times within the last M evaluations. Omit for consecutive mode. Must satisfy `alerting_check_times` <= M <= 10000.

recovery_check_times.description: Recover after the recovery condition is met this many times; minimum 1 when enabled.

severity.description: Severity of any-data alerts, case-sensitive; required when enabled.

recovery_mode.description: How recovery is decided (lifecycle v2); required when enabled. `data_absent` = recover when the query returns no data; `recovery` is not allowed. `recovery_query_match` = recover when the `recovery.expr` query expression evaluates true; only a single query (`name=A`) is allowed. `manual` = never recover automatically; alerts need manual handling, no recovery event is pushed, and `recovery` is not allowed.

recovery.description: Recovery evaluation config. Required (with non-empty `recovery.expr`) only when `recovery_mode` is `recovery_query_match`; must be omitted for the other modes.

enabled.description: Whether the per-series no-data check is enabled: series that previously reported data trigger an alert when data disappears.

severity.description: Severity of no-data alerts, case-sensitive; required when the per-series check is enabled.

alert_on_empty_result.description: Whether to alert when all queries return empty results (global empty-result check).

alert_on_empty_result_severity.description: Severity of empty-result alerts, case-sensitive; only takes effect and is required when `alert_on_empty_result` is on.

alerting_check_times.description: Fire after the alert condition is met this many times; when enabled, minimum 1 and maximum 10000. Combined with `alerting_window_size` it means at least N hits within the last M evaluations.

alerting_window_size.description: Optional sliding window size M: fire only when the condition is met at least `alerting_check_times` times within the last M evaluations. Omit for consecutive mode. Must satisfy `alerting_check_times` <= M <= 10000.

recovery_check_times.description: Recover after the recovery condition is met this many times; minimum 1 when enabled.

end_mode.description: How a no-data alert ends (lifecycle v2); required when enabled. `data_reappears` = recover when data reappears. `data_reappears_or_timeout` = end when data reappears or after `auto_close_after_seconds` seconds, whichever comes first; requires the per-series no-data check and a positive `auto_close_after_seconds`. `manual` = never end automatically; alerts need manual handling and no recovery event is pushed. For `data_reappears` and `manual`, `auto_close_after_seconds` must be 0.

auto_close_after_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before auto-closing. Allowed and required to be positive only when `end_mode` is `data_reappears_or_timeout`; must be 0 for the other modes.

AlertRuleRecoveryQueryV2.description: Recovery evaluation configuration for lifecycle v2.

expr.description: Recovery condition expression: a threshold expression (e.g. `$A < 90`) in `expression_match` mode, a query expression in `recovery_query_match` mode. Required and non-empty when the corresponding mode is enabled.

value_fields.description: Numeric result fields the recovery expression references as `$A.<field>`; same semantics as a query's `value_fields`. Not returned when empty.

args.description: Datasource-specific parameters for the recovery query; keys follow the same `<datasource>.<param>` convention as a query's `args`. Not returned when empty.

InvestigationTarget.description: Alert-event drill-down entry. A deliberately closed tagged union: new kinds require explicit server support, and unknown fields inside a target are rejected.

kind.description: Entry kind: `dashboard` opens a dashboard panel, `query` opens an Explore query. It decides whether `dashboard` or `query` must be supplied; supplying the other one is rejected.

time_range.description: Window around the event time, required on every saved entry. A zero-length window is rejected; defaults belong to the editor.

query.description: Configuration for the `query` kind; required when `kind` is `query`, and rejected when `kind` is `dashboard`.

dashboard.description: Configuration for the `dashboard` kind; required when `kind` is `dashboard`.

DashboardInvestigationTarget.description: Configuration of a dashboard drill-down entry.

dashboard_id.description: Target dashboard ID; must be a canonical UUIDv7.

target_id.description: Panel ID inside the dashboard; must be a canonical UUIDv7. Optional.

variables.description: Dashboard variable values, keyed by variable name. Values may reference event labels through `{{ }}` templates; defaults to an empty object.

InvestigationTimeRange.description: Window around the alert event time, expressed as two offsets. Both directions must be non-negative and at least one must be greater than zero, so an entry never resolves to an empty window.

before_seconds.description: Seconds to look back from the event time.

after_seconds.description: Seconds to look forward from the event time, so behaviour after the event stays visible.

QueryInvestigationTarget.description: Explore query used by a `query` drill-down entry. The expression may reference event labels through `{{ }}` templates, while `args` values may not.

datasource_id.description: Data source the query runs against.

DashboardQuery.description: Query payload shared by dashboards and drill-down entries.

mode.description: Evaluation mode: `instant` evaluates at a single timestamp, `range` evaluates a stepped series, `window` returns raw rows inside a time window.

expr.description: Query expression in the target data source's language. May reference event labels through `{{ }}` templates.

args.description: Named query arguments; defaults to an empty object. Values are passed through verbatim and must not contain `{{ }}` templates.

min_step_seconds.description: Minimum step, in seconds. Only accepted when `mode` is `range`, and must be greater than zero; omit or pass null to let the server decide.

DashboardDefinition.description: Complete dashboard payload stored as a portable `dashboard.v1` document. Unknown keys, duplicate keys, NaN/Inf, over-range numbers and trailing values are rejected; the serialized form must stay within 1 MiB.

title.description: Dashboard title, 1–189 Unicode code points after trimming.

description.description: Optional description, at most 1024 Unicode code points.

refresh_interval.description: Auto-refresh cadence applied by the console: `off` disables auto-refresh; `30s` = every 30 seconds; `1m` = every minute; `5m` = every 5 minutes.

variables.description: Dashboard variables, at most 20. Names must be unique within the definition and match the variable-name pattern.

tabs.description: Tabs, 1–10. Every tab title is unique and every tab or section ID must be a canonical UUIDv7 used only once across the definition.

DashboardRelativeTimeRange.description: Relative time window. `from` is one of the fixed presets the validator accepts; `to` is always the literal string `now`.

from.description: Start offset relative to `to`: `now-15m` = 15 minutes ago; `now-30m` = 30 minutes ago; `now-1h` = 1 hour ago; `now-3h` = 3 hours ago; `now-6h` = 6 hours ago; `now-12h` = 12 hours ago; `now-24h` = 24 hours ago; `now-7d` = 7 days ago.

to.description: End of the window; only `now` is accepted.

DashboardTab.description: A top-level tab. Panels can sit directly on the tab (`top_panels`) or inside sections.

id.description: Canonical UUIDv7 identifying the tab; unique across the definition.

title.description: Tab title, 1–189 Unicode code points. Unique among tabs.

top_panels.description: Panels placed directly on the tab, at most 30.

sections.description: Sections on the tab, at most 10.

DashboardSection.description: A collapsible group of panels inside a tab.

id.description: Canonical UUIDv7 identifying the section; unique across the definition.

collapsed.description: Whether the section renders collapsed by default.

panels.description: Panels in the section, at most 30.

DashboardPanel.description: A single visualization. Panels must not overlap inside the same container; the 24-column grid is validated on save.

id.description: Canonical UUIDv7 identifying the panel; unique across the definition.

queries.description: Queries in the panel. `time_series` accepts 1–26, `text` and `incident_list` accept none, every other kind accepts exactly one.

DashboardGridPosition.description: 24-column grid placement. `x` and `y` are zero-based; `x + w` must not exceed 24.

DashboardDatasourceRef.description: Points a panel or query variable at a datasource — either a fixed ID or a datasource variable evaluated at render time.

kind.description: `fixed` uses `datasource_id`; `variable` resolves `name` against a datasource variable.

datasource_id.description: Datasource ID. Required when `kind` is `fixed`, forbidden when `kind` is `variable`.

name.description: Datasource variable name. Required when `kind` is `variable`, forbidden when `kind` is `fixed`.

DashboardPanelQuery.description: One query inside a panel. `ref_id` labels the series in the panel and must be unique within the panel.

ref_id.description: Single uppercase letter (A–Z) naming the query inside its panel.

legend_alias.description: Optional legend label; supports the same variable templates as `expr`.

DashboardVariable.description: A dashboard variable. Pick the arm with `kind`.

DashboardDatasourceVariable.description: Datasource selector variable. Its candidates are the account's datasources of `datasource_type`.

kind.description: Variable kind discriminator; always `datasource`, selecting a datasource.

name.description: Variable name used in `{{ }}` templates, at most 64 characters.

label.description: Optional display label; falls back to `name`.

datasource_type.description: Datasource type the candidates are drawn from.

name_patterns.description: Wildcard patterns narrowing the candidates; empty means every datasource of the type.

default_datasource_id.description: Default datasource ID. Without a usable default the runtime picks the first candidate by name, then ID.

DashboardCustomVariable.description: Variable whose candidates come from a fixed list supplied inline.

kind.description: Variable kind discriminator; always `custom`, with candidates from a fixed list supplied inline.

name.description: Variable name used in `{{ }}` templates, at most 64 characters.

label.description: Optional display label; falls back to `name`.

options.description: Candidate list, 1–1000 entries. Values must be non-empty, unique and must not be `$__all`.

DashboardQueryVariable.description: Variable whose candidates are resolved by running a query against a datasource.

kind.description: Variable kind discriminator; always `query`, with candidates resolved by running a query against a datasource.

name.description: Variable name used in `{{ }}` templates, at most 64 characters.

label.description: Optional display label; falls back to `name`.

refresh.description: When the candidates are recomputed: `on_dashboard_load` = once when the dashboard loads; `on_time_range_change` = every time the time range changes.

mode.description: Selection cardinality: `single` makes the resolved selection hold exactly one value; `multi` allows multiple values.

include_all.description: When true the variable also offers an `all` selection.

DashboardSelection.description: A concrete selection of variable values. An empty `values` array is valid wire input and means unresolved — the server never substitutes a default for it.

kind.description: `values` selects the listed entries, `all` selects everything (only allowed when `include_all` is true).

values.description: Selected values, unique and never `$__all`. Must be empty when `kind` is `all`.

DashboardCandidate.description: One selectable option of a custom variable.

DashboardVariableQuery.description: Variable query. Pick the arm with `kind`; the arm must match the referenced datasource type.

kind.description: Query kind discriminator; always `prometheus`, a label-values query against Prometheus.

metric.description: Optional metric used to restrict the series considered.

label_filters.description: Optional matchers narrowing the series before label values are read.

op.description: Matcher operator: `=` = equals; `!=` = not equals; `=~` = regex match; `!~` = regex does-not-match.

value.description: Matcher value; may reference other variables through `{{ }}`.

DashboardSQLVariableQuery.description: SQL query returning one column of candidates.

kind.description: Query kind discriminator; always `sql`, a SQL query returning one column of candidates.

expr.description: SQL statement; may reference other variables through `{{ }}`.

args.description: Named query arguments; defaults to an empty object.

text_field.description: Column used as the candidate label; defaults to the value column.

value_field.description: Column used as the candidate value.

DashboardLogsVariableQuery.description: Logs query returning one field's values as candidates.

kind.description: Query kind discriminator; always `logs`, a logs query returning one field's values as candidates.

expr.description: Logs query expression; may reference other variables through `{{ }}`.

args.description: Named query arguments; defaults to an empty object.

field.description: Log field whose values become candidates.

DashboardVizConfig.description: Visualization configuration. `kind` selects the arm and therefore which sibling config object is required; `time_series` also carries the shared numeric options.

kind.description: Visualization kind discriminator; always `time_series`.

options.description: Open options object for the chosen visualization kind; the only part of the definition that round-trips losslessly. Missing or null normalizes to `{}`.

unit.description: Display unit for the panel's numeric values: `unitless` = raw number; `ratio` = fraction of 1; `percent` = percentage; `milliseconds` = duration in milliseconds; `seconds` = duration in seconds; `bytes` = size in bytes; `bits` = size in bits; `count_per_second` = per-second count; `bytes_per_second` = bytes per second; `bits_per_second` = bits per second.

decimals.description: Fixed decimal places; omit or send null to let the renderer decide.

kind.description: Visualization kind discriminator; always `table`.

options.description: Open options object for the chosen visualization kind; the only part of the definition that round-trips losslessly. Missing or null normalizes to `{}`.

column_options.description: Per-column display overrides keyed by field name, at most 100 entries.

sort.description: Initial sort keys; fields must be unique.

link_columns.description: Drill-down links rendered as table columns. Together with per-column links a table allows at most 5.

kind.description: Visualization kind discriminator; always `stat`.

options.description: Open options object for the chosen visualization kind; the only part of the definition that round-trips losslessly. Missing or null normalizes to `{}`.

unit.description: Display unit for the panel's numeric values: `unitless` = raw number; `ratio` = fraction of 1; `percent` = percentage; `milliseconds` = duration in milliseconds; `seconds` = duration in seconds; `bytes` = size in bytes; `bits` = size in bits; `count_per_second` = per-second count; `bytes_per_second` = bytes per second; `bits_per_second` = bits per second.

decimals.description: Fixed decimal places; omit or send null to let the renderer decide.

value_fields.description: Fields reduced to the displayed values.

reducer.description: Reduction applied across the returned rows: `last_non_null` = most recent non-null value; `min` = minimum; `max` = maximum; `mean` = average; `sum` = sum.

kind.description: Visualization kind discriminator; always `bar`.

options.description: Open options object for the chosen visualization kind; the only part of the definition that round-trips losslessly. Missing or null normalizes to `{}`.

unit.description: Display unit for the panel's numeric values: `unitless` = raw number; `ratio` = fraction of 1; `percent` = percentage; `milliseconds` = duration in milliseconds; `seconds` = duration in seconds; `bytes` = size in bytes; `bits` = size in bits; `count_per_second` = per-second count; `bytes_per_second` = bytes per second; `bits_per_second` = bits per second.

decimals.description: Fixed decimal places; omit or send null to let the renderer decide.

kind.description: Visualization kind discriminator; always `gauge`.

options.description: Open options object for the chosen visualization kind; the only part of the definition that round-trips losslessly. Missing or null normalizes to `{}`.

unit.description: Display unit for the panel's numeric values: `unitless` = raw number; `ratio` = fraction of 1; `percent` = percentage; `milliseconds` = duration in milliseconds; `seconds` = duration in seconds; `bytes` = size in bytes; `bits` = size in bits; `count_per_second` = per-second count; `bytes_per_second` = bytes per second; `bits_per_second` = bits per second.

decimals.description: Fixed decimal places; omit or send null to let the renderer decide.

value_fields.description: Fields reduced to the gauge value.

reducer.description: Reduction applied across the returned rows: `last_non_null` = most recent non-null value; `min` = minimum; `max` = maximum; `mean` = average; `sum` = sum.

max.description: Scale upper bound; must exceed `min` when both are set.

kind.description: Visualization kind discriminator; always `logs`.

options.description: Open options object for the chosen visualization kind; the only part of the definition that round-trips losslessly. Missing or null normalizes to `{}`.

display_fields.description: Log fields rendered for each row.

kind.description: Visualization kind discriminator; always `text`.

options.description: Open options object for the chosen visualization kind; the only part of the definition that round-trips losslessly. Missing or null normalizes to `{}`.

markdown.description: Markdown body, at most 64 KiB. Only a restricted node set (headings, lists, tables, links, code) survives validation.

DashboardIncidentListViz.description: Incident-list panel. The rows are filled by the client from the Flashduty incident API, so the panel runs no queries and needs no datasource.

kind.description: Visualization kind discriminator; always `incident_list`.

options.description: Open options object for the chosen visualization kind; the only part of the definition that round-trips losslessly. Missing or null normalizes to `{}`.

DashboardThreshold.description: Colour threshold for a numeric value. At least one of `warning`/`critical` is required, and with both set the pair must be ordered according to `mode`.

mode.description: Direction of the comparison: `higher_is_worse` = values at or above the bound breach it; `lower_is_worse` = values at or below the bound breach it.

DashboardColumnOption.description: Per-column display override for a table.

display_name.description: Header text replacing the raw field name.

hidden.description: Hide the column; omit to keep it visible.

unit.description: Unit override for the column: `unitless` = raw number; `ratio` = fraction of 1; `percent` = percentage; `milliseconds` = duration in milliseconds; `seconds` = duration in seconds; `bytes` = size in bytes; `bits` = size in bits; `count_per_second` = per-second count; `bytes_per_second` = bytes per second; `bits_per_second` = bits per second.

threshold_display.description: How the threshold is painted: `text` = colours the cell text; `background` = colours the cell background.

DashboardDataLink.description: Drill-down link from a table column or bar panel into another dashboard. The target dashboard must exist and the mapping sources must match the source panel's shape.

target_id.description: Optional tab, section or panel ID to focus in the target dashboard.

pass_time.description: When true the current time range is forwarded to the target.

variable_mappings.description: Maps target variable names to a source value such as a column or a source variable.

DashboardLinkMapping.description: One entry of a drill-down variable mapping.

source.description: Where the value comes from: `variable` = a dashboard variable; `row_column` = a table column (requires `column`); `category` = the bar category; `series` = the series name; `value` = the value itself. `category`, `series` and `value` are only valid for bar panels.

column.description: Source column name; required when `source` is `row_column`.

name.description: Source dashboard variable name; required when `source` is `variable`.

DashboardActor.description: Account member recorded as the creator, updater or revision author.

id.description: Member ID.

name.description: Member display name.

DashboardResource.description: A stored dashboard: its identity, revision counter, placement and full definition. `revision` increments on every accepted write and must be echoed back as `expected_revision` for the next mutation.

dashboard_id.description: Canonical UUIDv7 assigned by the caller at creation time.

schema_version.description: Wire schema version of `definition`; only `dashboard.v1` is accepted.

folder_breadcrumb.description: Folder names from the root down to `folder_id`.

DashboardListItem.description: One row of a dashboard listing. Carries the summary fields only — call the get endpoint for the full definition.

DashboardListOutput.description: A page of dashboards plus the total matching count.

total.description: Total number of matching dashboards across all pages.

DashboardTrashItem.description: One row of the trash listing.

folder_id.description: Folder the dashboard sat in when deleted.

revision.description: Revision the dashboard had when deleted.

DashboardTrashListOutput.description: A page of deleted dashboards. Entries older than the 30-day retention window are purged.

DashboardUpdateOutput.description: Result of an update or move. `changed` is false when the write was a no-op — the canonical serialized definition matched the stored one byte for byte, in which case `resource` still describes the unchanged dashboard.

changed.description: Whether the stored dashboard actually changed.

DashboardDeleteOutput.description: Result of moving a dashboard to the trash.

DashboardRevisionItem.description: One entry of the revision history. The server keeps the most recent 20 revisions including the current one.

folder_id.description: Folder the dashboard sat in at that revision.

message.description: Optional commit message; at most 1024 Unicode code points.

DashboardRevisionResource.description: A historical revision with its full definition.

schema_version.description: Wire schema version of `definition`; only `dashboard.v1` is accepted.

folder_id.description: Folder the dashboard sat in at that revision.

DashboardOutline.description: Structural outline of a dashboard — titles, breadcrumbs and visualization kinds, without queries or definitions. Pass `target_id` to narrow the outline to one tab, section or panel.

name.description: Variable name.

kind.description: Variable kind: `datasource` = selects a datasource; `custom` = fixed inline list; `query` = resolved by running a query.

DashboardOutlineTab.description: Tab entry in an outline, with its breadcrumb.

id.description: Tab ID.

breadcrumb.description: Dashboard title followed by the tab title.

top_panels.description: Panels placed directly on the tab.

id.description: Section ID.
Panel ID.

breadcrumb.description: Full path of titles from the dashboard down to the panel.

datasource_type.description: Datasource type the panel queries; empty when the panel has no datasource (text panels).

DashboardOutlineVizConfig.description: Visualization kind of an outlined panel.

kind.description: Visualization kind: `time_series` = time series; `table` = table; `stat` = single value; `bar` = bar chart; `gauge` = gauge; `logs` = log stream; `text` = Markdown text; `incident_list` = incident list.

DashboardSort.description: A sort key accepted by the listing endpoints. `field` must be one of the allowed fields for that endpoint and fields must be unique; at most two keys are accepted.

field.description: `title` is available everywhere; `updated_at` only on list/search, `deleted_at` only on the trash listing.

DashboardCreateRequest.description: Create a dashboard. The caller supplies the ID, so a retry after a timeout returns `DashboardIDConflict` rather than silently creating a second dashboard.

schema_version.description: Wire schema version; only `dashboard.v1` is accepted.

folder_id.description: Folder the dashboard is created in. Must be a folder the caller can write.

DashboardOutlineRequest.description: Request an outline, optionally narrowed to one tab, section or panel.

target_id.description: Optional tab, section or panel ID. When set, the response keeps only the branch that contains it, and an unknown ID returns `TargetNotFound`.

DashboardUpdateRequest.description: Replace a dashboard's definition. The whole definition is sent, not a patch; `expected_revision` makes the write compare-and-swap.

schema_version.description: Wire schema version; only `dashboard.v1` is accepted.

expected_revision.description: Revision the caller last read. The write fails with `DashboardRevisionConflict` unless it still matches the stored revision.

message.description: Optional revision message, at most 1024 Unicode code points. Stored with the revision and never returned by this endpoint.

DashboardMoveRequest.description: Move a dashboard to another folder without touching its definition.

expected_revision.description: Revision the caller last read. The write fails with `DashboardRevisionConflict` unless it still matches the stored revision.

DashboardDeleteRequest.description: Move a dashboard to the trash. The definition is retained for 30 days so the delete can be undone with the restore endpoint.

expected_revision.description: Revision the caller last read. The write fails with `DashboardRevisionConflict` unless it still matches the stored revision.

DashboardRestoreRequest.description: Restore a trashed dashboard, optionally into a different folder.

expected_revision.description: Revision the caller last read. The write fails with `DashboardRevisionConflict` unless it still matches the stored revision.

folder_id.description: Destination folder. Omit to restore to the original folder; when the original folder is no longer writable the call fails with `RestoreFolderRequired` and you must pass one.

DashboardListRequest.description: List the dashboards in one folder. Unlike search, `folder_id` is required.

query.description: Optional space-separated search words matched against title and description; at most 128 Unicode code points.

DashboardSearchRequest.description: Search dashboards across every folder the caller can read. The query must contain at least one word.

query.description: Space-separated search words; at least one word and at most 128 Unicode code points.

DashboardTrashListRequest.description: List trashed dashboards. Defaults to `deleted_at` descending.

sort.description: Sort keys; only `title` and `deleted_at` are accepted here.

DashboardAbsoluteTimeRange.description: Absolute evaluation window. Both bounds are Unix timestamps in milliseconds, `from_ms` must be less than `to_ms`, and neither may exceed the JavaScript safe integer limit.

DashboardRuntimeError.description: Per-variable or per-query failure. A failed arm does not fail the whole call.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure reason. Observed values include `invalid_request`, `variable_invalid`, `panel_missing`, `field_missing`, `datasource_permission_denied`, `timeout`, `panel_deadline`, `panel_canceled`, `canceled`, `overloaded`, `source_too_large`, `edge_unavailable`, `edge_upgrade_required`, `edge_version_unknown`, `mixed_edge_versions` and `internal`.

DashboardRuntimeDatasource.description: The datasource a runtime query was bound to.

id.description: Datasource ID.

name.description: Datasource name.

DashboardResolvedVariable.description: One resolved variable. An unreachable datasource, a bad expression or an empty result leaves `candidates` incomplete and fills `error` instead of failing the request.

name.description: Variable name.

kind.description: Variable kind: `datasource` = selects a datasource; `custom` = fixed inline list; `query` = resolved by running a query.

DashboardVariablesResolveRequest.description: Resolve every variable of a stored dashboard against a time range and the caller's current selections.

variables.description: Selections already made, keyed by variable name, at most 20 entries. Variables omitted here fall back to their stored defaults.

DashboardVariablesResolveResponse.description: Resolved variables plus the effective selection for each name.

selections.description: Effective selections keyed by variable name; only variables that resolved successfully appear.

DashboardResolvedQuery.description: One query bound to a concrete datasource with its variables substituted.

mode.description: Evaluation mode: `range` = a stepped time series; `instant` = a single point in time; `window` = raw rows inside a bounded time window.

expr.description: Expression with variable templates substituted.

args.description: Query arguments; empty object when none.

min_step_seconds.description: Minimum step in seconds; null when unset.

DashboardResolvedPanelQueries.description: Per-panel resolution result. `state` is `success` when every query resolved, `partial` when some did and `error` when none did.

state.description: Aggregate state of the panel's queries: `success` = every query resolved; `partial` = some resolved; `error` = none resolved.

DashboardQueriesResolveRequest.description: Resolve the queries of selected panels without executing them, so a client can preview datasource binding and variable substitution.

panel_ids.description: Panels to resolve, 1–100 unique IDs. A panel that does not exist yields an `error` arm rather than failing the call.

variables.description: Selections keyed by variable name, at most 20 entries.

DashboardQueriesResolveResponse.description: One entry per requested panel, in request order.

DashboardPanelRunBudget.description: Execution accounting for a panel run.

max_concurrency.description: Concurrency cap applied to the panel's queries.

DashboardPanelRunRef.description: Result of one query inside a panel run. The raw execution payload differs per datasource type and is passed through unmodified, so it is not schema-constrained here.

state.description: Per-query execution state: `success` = the query executed; `error` = the query failed; `incompatible` = the datasource accepted the call but the query mode or field selection does not fit the datasource type.

child_request_id.description: Request ID of the underlying datasource execution; use it when tracing a single query.

execution.description: Datasource-specific execution payload, passed through unmodified.

DashboardPanelRunRequest.description: Execute one panel against the stored dashboard. Omit `revision` to run the current revision; send it to have stale responses rejected.

revision.description: Revision guard; when set it must equal the current revision.

variables.description: Selections keyed by variable name, at most 20 entries.

max_data_points.description: Downsampling target, 2–5000 points; omit or send null for the server default of 100.

DashboardPanelRunResponse.description: Panel execution result. `run_state` aggregates the per-query states: `success` when all succeeded, `partial` when some did, otherwise `incompatible`, `cancelled` or `error`. The total response is capped at 8 MiB.

run_state.description: Aggregate state of the run: `success` = all queries succeeded; `partial` = some succeeded; `incompatible` = at least one query is incompatible with its datasource; `cancelled` = the run was cancelled; `error` = all queries failed.

refs.description: One entry per query in the panel.

DashboardDraftContext.description: Where an unsaved draft panel or variable set belongs. `existing` targets a stored dashboard, `new` a folder that does not contain one yet — the two are mutually exclusive.

kind.description: Draft context kind: `existing` = targets a stored dashboard (`dashboard_id` required); `new` = a folder that does not contain one yet (`folder_id` required).

DashboardVariablesPreviewRequest.description: Resolve a draft set of variables that is not stored in any dashboard yet.

selections.description: Selections keyed by variable name, at most 20 entries.

DashboardVariablesPreviewResponse.description: Resolved draft variables. There is no `dashboard_id` because nothing is persisted.

selections.description: Effective selections keyed by variable name.

DashboardPanelPreviewRequest.description: Execute a draft panel inline, without saving a dashboard revision. Subject to the same 1 MiB definition-size ceiling.

variables.description: Draft variables the panel may reference.

DashboardPanelPreviewResponse.description: Draft panel execution result. Same shape as a stored panel run, minus the dashboard identity.

run_state.description: Aggregate state of the run: `success` = all queries succeeded; `partial` = some succeeded; `incompatible` = at least one query is incompatible with its datasource; `cancelled` = the run was cancelled; `error` = all queries failed.

refs.description: One entry per query in the panel.

FolderItem.description: A monitor folder (监控节点). Folders form a tree; `parent_path` is the comma-separated ancestor ID list, so the caller can rebuild the tree and search it client-side.

id.description: Folder ID.

parent_id.description: Parent folder ID; 0 at the root.

parent_path.description: Comma-separated ancestor IDs from the root, excluding this folder; empty at the root.

team_id.description: Team the folder is scoped to; 0 when account-wide.

name.description: Folder name.

updater_id.description: Member ID of the last updater.
